title: Bit-level remainder identities and scoped bad-run implication

concepts.label: audited expansion claim boundary
concepts.note: A distinction between an exact Lean declaration, supporting proof substrate, finite checked instances, measurements, and any claim that would resolve an open Erdős problem.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED: badRun_pins_remainder pins the row-N remainder to a short interval when every row from N+1 through 3N+2 is bad and the terminal ceiling hypothesis holds.
open_antecedents: hbad: every row from N+1 through 3N+2 fails LargestSkipLateAt
statement_nodes.engine: iteration of the bit-level bad-row recurrence
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: No priority or novelty claim is made. This node records the exact scope needed for public claim hygiene.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The premise needs at least twelve consecutive bad rows in the relevant range; the audit found a maximum run of three in the measured data. The theorem therefore supplies no observed case.
